films.title: THE EPIC VIDEO
films.description: Swedish brand Epic Life Changing Device's 16-minute full-length links its European base with East Coast street skating. Simon Capdevila edited the film and shares camera duties with Steffen Austerheim, Jonathan Norberg and Eros Fagnani; six additional camera contributors are explicitly credited. The complete ten-skater appearance roster retains Joppe and Eirik Svensen as supporting appearances alongside the eight principal-billed riders.
creditNotes: The official upload supplies the complete order, Simon Capdevila's edit credit, four principal camera credits and six additional-camera credits.

Free Skate Mag independently repeats the appearance order and identifies Joppe with Eros Fagnani and Eirik Svensen with Steffen Austerheim; those two are preserved as supporting appearances rather than promoted to principal billing.
No formal director credit was found, so none is asserted.
films.locationNote: BE Skate Mag describes the film as connecting the Swedish brand's European roots with East Coast street skating; no city-level filming list was published.
films.historicalContext: Epic Life Changing Device's company full-length is a transatlantic team film, not the preceding Steffen Austerheim teaser/part that Free Skate Mag referenced in its release coverage.
films.artworkNotes: The official 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-15. It is a genuine fisheye street-skating frame from the exact company upload, with no misleading event or trailer text.

Independent release coverage classifies the upload as the Swedish brand's full-length, repeats the complete appearance order, identifies the two supporting appearances and confirms Simon Capdevila's edit plus the four main camera credits.
Independent coverage corroborates the ten-skater roster and the film's Swedish / European-to-East-Coast context.

films.title: The Civil Video
films.description: Civil Skateshop's first full-length is a 23-minute Rhode Island scene document filmed by Luke Franco, Kenny Borge and Dan McGrath. Civil's official billing highlights seven team riders, while the independently catalogued credits preserve 40 additional montage and community appearances for a complete 47-skater roster.
creditNotes: Civil's official upload names seven featured team riders, the three filmers and Lucky St. Angelo's thumbnail photo credit.

SkateVideoSite's independent section and montage catalog expands the roster to 47 named appearances. The additional 40 are retained as montage/community appearances and are not promoted to principal-part status.
No formal director or editor credit was found, so neither is asserted.
films.locationNote: Civil states that the entire video was filmed in Rhode Island; SkateVideoSite specifically catalogs Providence.
films.historicalContext: Civil opened in 2006 and described this release as its first proper shop full-length, documenting Rhode Island's local skate community after nearly two decades of shop activity.
premiereNotes: Civil's first-party announcement documents a free April 26, 2025 premiere, with the screening scheduled for 8:00 PM; the complete film was published online June 9, 2025.
physicalReleaseNotes: SkateVideoSite records a limited run of 50 DVD copies and lists an active Civil purchase link as of March 2026.
films.artworkNotes: The official 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-15. It is Lucky St. Angelo's vertically composed action photo of a Civil rider skating over a car, pillar-boxed within the standard player frame, and it matches the exact company upload.
